# docx plan reference

<!-- Generated by tools/schemagen from internal/docx/ops. Do not edit. -->

A docx plan is a JSON object in the grammar of the agent contract (`docs/contract.md`): `base` (the
`sha256:` hash of the document it was written against), `author`, `change_mode` (`track` or `direct`)
and `ops`, the operations in order. `docs/docx-plan.schema.json` is its JSON Schema. Plans are JSON
only. The operation names and fields are the contract's; each operation names the docxdriver 0.5.2
operation it runs as, which `tools/oracle` translates plans by for parity runs.

A rejected plan gets one diagnostic: `invalid_json` (syntax, with the position), `invalid_plan`
(an unknown, missing or mistyped field or a malformed value), `empty_plan`, `invalid_author`, or
`invalid_operation` (the first operation that breaks a rule below; `path` names the field).

Lengths are points in multiples of 0.05 (stored as twentieths of a point); indents may be
negative (-100000 to 100000), other lengths may not. Paragraph addresses are eight uppercase
hexadecimal digits or `$alias`; the other addresses are as `docs/contract.md`, section 6, gives them.

complex field runs; DirectOnly is refused in track mode; Untracked applies directly in both modes.

### text.replace

Tracked: w:del / w:ins (the author's own pending insertion is edited in place). Direct: replaced, no revision.

Change mode: Exact.

| Field | Type | Required | Values | Stored as |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `at` | ParagraphAddress | yes |  |  |
| `select` | string | yes |  |  |
| `with` | string Plain text: a tab is \t, a line break \n. An equation or other object in the selection (U+FFFC in select) must stay U+FFFC in `with`; one cannot be made or removed here. | yes |  |  |
| `occurrence` | integer | no |  |  |
| `all` | boolean Replace every match of `select` in the paragraph. Not with `occurrence`. | no (default `false`) |  |  |

| # | Rule message | Path |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | select must be non-empty | `select` |
| 2 | occurrence must be positive | `occurrence` |
| 3 | occurrence and all exclude each other | `all` |

### text.revise

Several exact replacements inside one bounded scope: the paragraph `at`, the unique `within` span (in `at`, or anywhere in the body when `at` is omitted), or the whole body. Every edit resolves against the scope as it stands when this operation starts. Tracked: w:del / w:ins per edit. Direct: replaced, no revision.

Change mode: Exact.

| Field | Type | Required | Values | Stored as |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `at` | ParagraphAddress | no |  |  |
| `within` | string | no |  |  |
| `occurrence` | integer | no |  |  |
| `edits` | list of TextEdit | yes |  |  |

| # | Rule message | Path |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | within must be non-empty when given | `within` |
| 2 | occurrence must be positive | `occurrence` |
| 3 | occurrence picks a within match; it requires within | `occurrence` |
| 4 | edits must list at least one replacement | `edits` |
| 5 | edits[N].select must be non-empty \| edits[N].occurrence must be positive \| edits[N] sets both all and occurrence; choose one | by value, e.g. `edits[1]` |

### text.insert

Insert `with` at an insertion point: just before or after the selected text, or at the start (`before`) or end (`after`) of the paragraph when `select` is omitted. Tracked: w:ins. Direct: inserted, no revision.

Change mode: Exact.

| Field | Type | Required | Values | Stored as |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `at` | ParagraphAddress | yes |  |  |
| `select` | string Insert just before or after this text; omitted, at the start (`before`) or end (`after`) of the paragraph. | no |  |  |
| `occurrence` | integer | no |  |  |
| `position` | InsertPosition | yes |  |  |
| `with` | string Plain text: a tab is \t, a line break \n; no U+FFFC. | yes |  |  |

| # | Rule message | Path |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | select must be non-empty; omit it to insert at the start or end of the paragraph | `select` |
| 2 | occurrence must be positive | `occurrence` |
| 3 | occurrence requires select | `occurrence` |

### paragraph.insert

One paragraph, or with a list `html`, one per item in list order. Each `html` value is one paragraph: either one block element, `<p>` or `<h1>`..`<h6>` as read shows it, whose style (the heading's tag, `data-style` or `class`) and paragraph CSS become the new paragraph's properties (its `id`, list marker and revision attributes, and an equation's `data-ref`, are ignored), or bare inline content, which is the content alone. Two block elements in one value, or a block element inside inline content, are refused: one paragraph per html value; use the list form for several. With `as`, a single paragraph is `$<as>`; for a list, `$<as>` is the group (expanded in paragraph lists, its first or last paragraph as an insert anchor) and item N is `$<as>_N`. Without `style`, a new paragraph takes the paragraph properties of a paragraph anchor (style, numbering, indents, spacing; not its mark's run properties, section properties or pending changes), as Word's Enter does: inserted into a list it is a list item. After a paragraph whose style names a different next style (a heading), it takes that style instead. Tracked: inserted content and paragraph mark; reject-all removes the paragraph. Direct: inserted, no revision.

Change mode: Exact.

| Field | Type | Required | Values | Stored as |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `at` | InsertAnchor | yes |  |  |
| `position` | InsertPosition | yes |  |  |
| `html` | ParagraphContent | no (default `""`) |  |  |
| `style` | string | no |  |  |
| `as` | string | no |  |  |

| # | Rule message | Path |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | invalid alias | `as` |
| 2 | an html list must not be empty | `html` |

### paragraph.delete

Tracked: content and paragraph mark deleted; accept-all leaves the following paragraph's id and properties as they were. A paragraph whose mark cannot join forward (the last of the body, one before a table, one ending a section) takes the previous paragraph's mark instead, as Word does: it gets that paragraph's properties (its own in a pPrChange) and keeps its section properties, and accept-all leaves the previous paragraph, with its id, in its place. Where no previous paragraph can join (a table or another author's mark revision before it) it is left empty. Direct: the same edit accepted, no revision.

Change mode: Exact.

| Field | Type | Required | Values | Stored as |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `at` | list of ParagraphAddress | yes |  |  |

| # | Rule message | Path |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | at must not be empty | `at` |

### list.set

Assign selected paragraphs to a new or existing list. `remove` explicitly suppresses inherited numbering. Tracked: w:pPrChange; rejecting it also removes the list definitions it added once nothing refers to them (definitions the input already left unreferenced stay). Direct: applied, no revision.

Change mode: Exact.

| Field | Type | Required | Values | Stored as |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `levels` | list of ListLevel | no |  |  |
| `at` | list of ParagraphAddress | yes |  |  |
| `num_id` | integer | no |  |  |
| `format` | string | no | `bullet`, `decimal`, `lowerLetter`, `upperLetter`, `lowerRoman`, `upperRoman` | w:ST_NumberFormat |
| `level` | integer | no (default `0`) |  |  |
| `start` | integer | no |  |  |
| `remove` | boolean | no (default `false`) |  |  |

| # | Rule message | Path |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | levels requires a new list with 1..9 definitions covering the selected level | `levels` |
| 2 | invalid list level format, label, start or restart ancestor \| list indentation is out of range \| list labels may only reference this level or ancestor %1..%9 counters \| invalid list marker font or six-digit RGB color | by value, e.g. `levels[0].marker_color` |
| 3 | list.set requires paragraphs, level 0..8 and IDs/starts in 1..2147483647 | by value, e.g. `num_id` |
| 4 | list.set remove cannot be combined with list settings | `remove` |
| 5 | unsupported list.set format | `format` |
| 6 | format cannot restyle an existing list; create a new list | `format` |

### table.insert

A `rows` × `columns` grid of new cells. `cells` fills them row by row with the inline content `paragraph.insert`'s `html` accepts; missing trailing rows and cells stay empty. With `as`, cell row N column M is the paragraph alias `$<as>_rNcM` for later operations. Tracked: an inserted table (every row w:trPr/w:ins, cell content w:ins); refused as the last block of a table cell. Direct: inserted, no revision.

Change mode: Exact.

| Field | Type | Required | Values | Stored as |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `at` | ParagraphAddress | yes |  |  |
| `position` | InsertPosition | yes |  |  |
| `rows` | integer | yes |  |  |
| `columns` | integer | yes |  |  |
| `cells` | list of list of string | no |  |  |
| `as` | string | no |  |  |

| # | Rule message | Path |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | table.insert dimensions must be 1..100 | by value, e.g. `rows` |
| 2 | invalid alias | `as` |
| 3 | cells has N rows but the table has R: remove cells[R..] (row R+1[ to row N]) | by value, e.g. `cells` |
| 4 | cells[I] (row I+1) has N cells but the table has C columns: remove cells[I][C..] (column C+1[ to column N]) | by value, e.g. `cells[1]` |

### revision.accept

Accept revisions: one (`at: "revision:7"`), all of them (`all`), or those of the listed body paragraphs (`at` a paragraph list: their content, paragraph mark and property changes, their text boxes' included; not row, cell or table changes); `author` narrows `all` or the paragraphs to that author's revisions. Accepting a paragraph mark's revision can join the paragraph with the next one. Settles revisions in both change modes; it writes none.

Change mode: Untracked.

| Field | Type | Required | Values | Stored as |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `at` | RevisionScope One revision (`revision:7`), or the body paragraphs whose revisions are settled. Not with `all`. | no |  |  |
| `all` | boolean Every revision of the document. | no (default `false`) |  |  |
| `author` | RevisionAuthor Only this author's revisions (with all or paragraphs). | no |  |  |

| # | Rule message | Path |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | give at (a revision or paragraphs) or all: true; author narrows either | `at` |
| 2 | at and all exclude each other | `all` |
| 3 | at must name at least one paragraph when given | `at` |
| 4 | author narrows all or a list of paragraphs, not one revision | `author` |

### revision.reject

Reject revisions: one (`at: "revision:7"`), all of them (`all`), or those of the listed body paragraphs (`at` a paragraph list: their content, paragraph mark and property changes, their text boxes' included; not row, cell or table changes); `author` narrows `all` or the paragraphs to that author's revisions. Rejecting a paragraph mark's revision can join the paragraph with the next one. Settles revisions in both change modes; it writes none.

Change mode: Untracked.

| Field | Type | Required | Values | Stored as |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `at` | RevisionScope One revision (`revision:7`), or the body paragraphs whose revisions are settled. Not with `all`. | no |  |  |
| `all` | boolean Every revision of the document. | no (default `false`) |  |  |
| `author` | RevisionAuthor Only this author's revisions (with all or paragraphs). | no |  |  |

| # | Rule message | Path |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | give at (a revision or paragraphs) or all: true; author narrows either | `at` |
| 2 | at and all exclude each other | `all` |
| 3 | at must name at least one paragraph when given | `at` |
| 4 | author narrows all or a list of paragraphs, not one revision | `author` |

### revision.convert_to_formatting

Turn tracked changes into amendment formatting (37 CFR 1.121): an insertion's text stays, underlined; a deletion's text comes back, struck through; no revision is left. A deleted paragraph mark stays (the paragraph's struck text keeps its own line); an inserted paragraph stays with its text underlined; inserted and deleted table rows stay, their text underlined or struck. Formatting, table and section property changes have no amendment form and are accepted. Moves convert as deletion (source) and insertion (destination). Where struck and underlined text meet with a word character on both sides (a replaced word, whose redline shares one surrounding space), one plain space goes between them: "~~attached~~ <u>secured</u>", as in MPEP 714 examples; none is added next to whitespace or untouched punctuation, or for a pure insertion or deletion. Existing underline and strike are kept. `all` converts every revision, `at` one revision (`revision:7`) or those in the listed body paragraphs, `author` those of one author. Settles revisions, so it writes none of its own in either change mode.

Change mode: Untracked.

| Field | Type | Required | Values | Stored as |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `at` | RevisionScope One revision (`revision:7`), or the paragraphs whose revisions are converted. Not with `all`. | no |  |  |
| `all` | boolean Every revision of the body and of the headers and footers. | no (default `false`) |  |  |
| `author` | RevisionAuthor Only this author's revisions (with all or paragraphs). | no |  |  |

| # | Rule message | Path |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | give at (a revision or paragraphs) or all: true; author narrows either | (the operation) |
| 2 | at and all exclude each other | `all` |
| 3 | at must name at least one paragraph when given | `at` |
| 4 | author narrows all or a list of paragraphs, not one revision | `author` |

## Intended differences from docxdriver 0.5.2

Parity with docxdriver's plan parsing is on whether a plan is accepted and, when it is refused, the
code (docs/plan.md, decision 2); names, fields, messages and paths are the contract's. The
differential test (internal/docx/ops/oracle_test.go) translates each recorded docxdriver plan into
the contract's grammar (ops.FromOracle), compares the outcome with the recorded oracle result and
fails on any difference not listed here.

| Class | Why |
| --- | --- |
| positional-form | serde accepts a struct (the plan, a format, an edit) or an internally or adjacently tagged enum (an operation, a table edit, a line spacing) written as a JSON array of its fields in declaration order. The plan schema allows only objects, and a positional plan is unreadable and breaks silently when a field is added, so the Go parser refuses arrays where objects are expected. |
| enum-map-form | serde accepts a unit enum value (change_mode, position, highlight, …) written as a one-key map {"track": null}, and reports an empty or larger map as "expected map with a single key". The schema allows only the string; the Go parser refuses maps with "invalid type: map, expected a string". |
| unit-variant-members | serde ignores members next to the tag of a unit variant ({"unit": "auto", "value": 3}, {"kind": "delete", "x": 1}) despite deny_unknown_fields, so a mistyped edit is silently dropped. The Go parser refuses them as unknown fields. |
| latex-equation | The docx CLI takes equations as LaTeX only (planner decision): equation.replace has a required `latex` field where docxdriver's replace_equation has `mathml`, and canonical JSON holds the canonical LaTeX (math.CanonicalLaTeX), and malformed LaTeX is an invalid_operation at `latex`. A docxdriver plan with `mathml` gets the unknown-field error; docxdriver refuses `latex` the same way. The schema's replace_equation variant differs accordingly. |
| variant-index | serde accepts an integer tag as a variant index ({"kind": 3} is delete_columns). The schema allows only names; the Go parser refuses integers as it refuses other non-string tags. |
| contract-addresses | The contract names a section by one address (`at`: section:N, section:final or a section alias) where docxdriver has two fields, a number (`section`) and a handle (`section_handle`), and refuses a plan that gives both. FromOracle cannot say "both" in the contract's grammar, so it keeps the two docxdriver fields and the plan is refused as having unknown fields (invalid_plan) where docxdriver refuses it by rule (invalid_operation). |
| null-refused | serde reads null as an absent optional field. The contract's decoder (internal/cli, shared with pptx) refuses null everywhere: a plan leaves a field out instead, so a null that was meant as a value is never silently dropped. |
| duplicate-keys | serde_json keeps the last of duplicate object keys, so {"select":"x","select":"z"} means z. The contract's parser refuses duplicate keys (invalid_json): which one was meant cannot be known. |
| nesting-limit | serde_json stops at 127 levels of nesting (its recursion limit is 128 including the outermost value's frame); the shared parser takes 128 levels and then refuses the value as a plan (invalid_plan). Either way the text is refused. |
| revision-selection | docxdriver's convert_revisions_to_formatting has a required `target` (all, one id or one author); the contract says the same with three optional fields (`all`, `at`, `author`), so a plan that says neither `at` nor `all` breaks a rule (invalid_operation) where docxdriver's is missing a field (invalid_plan). |
